articles.summary: Enterprises choose security tools for their expertise in the areas that matter to their business. Each tool detects problems in its domain and judges them with the context it holds. The context that decides how much a finding matters to a particular organization is spread across many systems: what the resource does for the business, who owns it, what data it holds, what else in the environment it connects to, and what other tools have found on it.The Sola Security Brain closes that gap.
articles.title: Resolving the Enterprise: Unified Third-Party Findings in the Enterprise Security Brain

articles.summary: Security teams spend nearly as much time hunting down resource owners as they do analyzing risk. Static tags and CMDB entries go stale the moment an engineer switches teams, leaving alert remediation stranded. But true ownership lives in the digital footprint people leave every day—Git commits, PR reviews, audit logs, and tickets. Our latest paper details an agentic architecture that mines these implicit signals across your existing tools to identify who actually builds, maintains, and answers for your cloud resources.
articles.title: Agentic attribution of cloud resource ownership: finding owners in the records you already keep
